sections.theory:
ii. The Structure of Silicon dioxide

Silicon atoms are bigger than carbon atoms, which mean that silicon – oxygen bond will be long as compared to carbon–oxygen bond. The ‘p’ orbital on the silicon and the oxygen are not quite close enough together to allow enough side wise overlap to give us a stable ‘π’ bond. Thus, silicon oxygen bond is a single bond –

Figure 13.8 Structure of Silicon dioxide.

The SiO₂ molecule is a giant covalent structure in which each silicon atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms through single covalent bonds whereas each oxygen atom is bonded to two silicon atoms.

13.4.6.2 Acid Base Behaviour of Group IV Oxides

The oxides of group – IVA elements are acidic, but their acidity decreases as we move down the group. Acid – base reactions of these oxides are given below.

i. Group–IVA monoxides

Carbon monoxide is treated as neutral oxide but it is slightly acidic. It does not react with water. It reacts with hot and concentrated sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to produce sodium methanoate (HCOONa).

CO(g) + NaOH(aq) → HCOONa(aq)

Germanium, tin and lead monoxides are amphoteric oxides. They can act as an acid as well as a base.

As a base:

SnO(s) + 2HCl(aq) → SnCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l)

As an acid:

SnO(s) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SnO₂(aq) + H₂O(l)

ii. Group – IVA dioxides

Carbon dioxide is a slight acidic oxide. It reacts with water to a slight extent to produce hydrogen ions and hydrogencarbonate ions.

CO₂(g) + H₂O(l) → H⁺(aq) + HCO₃⁻(aq)

Carbon dioxide reacts with cold sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to give either sodium carbonate or sodium hydrogencarbonate solution, depending on the proportion.

CO₂(g) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂CO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

or

CO₂(g) + NaOH(aq) → NaHCO₃(aq)

Silicon dioxide is weakly acidic. It reacts with hot and concentrated sodium hydroxide to give sodium silicate. However, it does not react with water due to its strong covalent bonds.

SiO₂(s) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SiO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

Germanium, tin and lead dioxides are amphoteric oxides. They can act as an acid as well as a base.

As a base:

SnO₂(s) + 4HCl(aq) → SnCl₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l)

For germanium and tin dioxides, hot and concentrated hydrochloric acid is used. However, for lead dioxide, cold hydrochloric acid is used. This is because, lead dioxide will decompose if the temperature increases.

As an acid:

SnO₂(s) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SnO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

For all reactions, hot and concentrated sodium hydroxide is used.

13.5 Group–VIIA Elements: Halogens

Group–VIIA comprise the elements fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), iodine (I), and astatine (At). The elements are collectively known as halogens due to their salts forming tendency. All these elements are non-metals.

13.5.1 Atomic and Physical Properties

Elements of Group – VIIA (halogens) possess seven electrons in the outermost (valence) shell, the characteristics feature being ‘ns²np⁵’ in the outer most shell. The elements and their atomic number etc. are given in Table 13.24.

کاربن ډای اکسایډ لږ تېزابي اکسایډ دی. دا له اوبو سره په لږه کچه تعامل کوي او د هایدروجن ایونونه او د هایدروجن کاربونېټ ایونونه جوړوي.

CO₂(g) + H₂O(l) → H⁺(aq) + HCO₃⁻(aq)

کاربن ډای اکسایډ له سړه سوډیم هایدروکسایډ (NaOH) سره تعامل کوي او د تناسب له مخې د سوډیم کاربونېټ یا سوډیم هایدروجن کاربونېټ محلول جوړوي.

CO₂(g) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂CO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

یا

CO₂(g) + NaOH(aq) → NaHCO₃(aq)

سیلیکان ډای اکسایډ کمزوری تېزابي دی. له ګرم او غلیظ سوډیم هایدروکسایډ سره تعامل کوي او سوډیم سیلیکېټ جوړوي. خو د خپلو پیاوړو کووالنټ تړونونو له امله له اوبو سره تعامل نه کوي.

SiO₂(s) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SiO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

د جرمانیم، ټین او سرب ډای اکسایډونه امفوتېریک اکسایډونه دي. هغوی د تېزاب او اساس دواړو په توګه عمل کولای شي.

د اساس په توګه:

SnO₂(s) + 4HCl(aq) → SnCl₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l)

د جرمانیم او ټین د ډای اکسایډونو لپاره ګرم او غلیظ هایدروکلوریک تېزاب کارېږي. خو د سرب ډای اکسایډ لپاره سړه هایدروکلوریک تېزاب کارېږي، ځکه که تودوخه لوړه شي، سرب ډای اکسایډ تجزیه کېږي.

د تېزاب په توګه:

SnO₂(s) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SnO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

د ټولو تعاملونو لپاره ګرم او غلیظ سوډیم هایدروکسایډ کارېږي.

13.5 د VIIA ګروپ عناصر: هالوجنونه

VIIA ګروپ فلورین (F)، کلورین (Cl)، برومین (Br)، ایوډین (I) او اسټاټین (At) رانغاړي. دا عناصر د مالګو د جوړولو د تمایل له امله په ګډه هالوجنونه بلل کېږي. دا ټول عناصر نافلزونه دي.

13.5.1 اټومي او فزیکي ځانګړنې

د VIIA ګروپ عناصر (هالوجنونه) په تر ټولو بهرني ظرفي پوښ کې اووه الکترونونه لري؛ په تر ټولو بهرني پوښ کې ns²np⁵ د هغوی ځانګړی صفت دی. عناصر، د هغوی اټومي شمېرې او نور په جدول 13.24 کې ورکړل شوي دي.

جدول 13.24 د عناصرو نښې، اټومي شمېرې او د هغوی الکتروني ترتیب
sections.content:
ii. The Structure of Silicon dioxide

Silicon atoms are bigger than carbon atoms, which mean that silicon – oxygen bond will be long as compared to carbon–oxygen bond. The ‘p’ orbital on the silicon and the oxygen are not quite close enough together to allow enough side wise overlap to give us a stable ‘π’ bond. Thus, silicon oxygen bond is a single bond –

Figure 13.8 Structure of Silicon dioxide.

The SiO₂ molecule is a giant covalent structure in which each silicon atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms through single covalent bonds whereas each oxygen atom is bonded to two silicon atoms.

13.4.6.2 Acid Base Behaviour of Group IV Oxides

The oxides of group – IVA elements are acidic, but their acidity decreases as we move down the group. Acid – base reactions of these oxides are given below.

i. Group–IVA monoxides

Carbon monoxide is treated as neutral oxide but it is slightly acidic. It does not react with water. It reacts with hot and concentrated sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to produce sodium methanoate (HCOONa).

CO(g) + NaOH(aq) → HCOONa(aq)

Germanium, tin and lead monoxides are amphoteric oxides. They can act as an acid as well as a base.

As a base:

SnO(s) + 2HCl(aq) → SnCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l)

As an acid:

SnO(s) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SnO₂(aq) + H₂O(l)

ii. Group – IVA dioxides

Carbon dioxide is a slight acidic oxide. It reacts with water to a slight extent to produce hydrogen ions and hydrogencarbonate ions.

CO₂(g) + H₂O(l) → H⁺(aq) + HCO₃⁻(aq)

Carbon dioxide reacts with cold sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to give either sodium carbonate or sodium hydrogencarbonate solution, depending on the proportion.

CO₂(g) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂CO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

or

CO₂(g) + NaOH(aq) → NaHCO₃(aq)

Silicon dioxide is weakly acidic. It reacts with hot and concentrated sodium hydroxide to give sodium silicate. However, it does not react with water due to its strong covalent bonds.

SiO₂(s) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SiO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

Germanium, tin and lead dioxides are amphoteric oxides. They can act as an acid as well as a base.

As a base:

SnO₂(s) + 4HCl(aq) → SnCl₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l)

For germanium and tin dioxides, hot and concentrated hydrochloric acid is used. However, for lead dioxide, cold hydrochloric acid is used. This is because, lead dioxide will decompose if the temperature increases.

As an acid:

SnO₂(s) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SnO₃(aq) + H₂O(l)

For all reactions, hot and concentrated sodium hydroxide is used.

13.5 Group–VIIA Elements: Halogens

Group–VIIA comprise the elements fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), iodine (I), and astatine (At). The elements are collectively known as halogens due to their salts forming tendency. All these elements are non-metals.

13.5.1 Atomic and Physical Properties

Elements of Group – VIIA (halogens) possess seven electrons in the outermost (valence) shell, the characteristics feature being ‘ns²np⁵’ in the outer most shell. The elements and their atomic number etc. are given in Table 13.24.
